The end-to-end charge test failed with "no active signing key selected" from identity-service/src/signer.ts. Root cause: during the "externalize secrets" refactor, both identity-service and ledger-service had their concrete signing key id blanked out (activeKid/trustedKid set to "") in their config files, with no fallback. The shared keyring still holds the material (including k_quartz), but neither service selected a key, so signSession threw before minting.

Anchor-dense memory confirmed the intended direction: (1) identity and ledger now read the active signing key id from env rather than a hardcoded default; (2) OPS-522 established k_quartz as the working/trusted key id that recovers verification.

Fix: updated identity-service/src/config.ts to read activeKid from process.env.MERIDIAN_SIGNING_KID (defaulting to "k_quartz"), and ledger-service/src/config.ts to read trustedKid from process.env.MERIDIAN_TRUSTED_KID (defaulting to "k_quartz"). Both services now select the same key (k_quartz) by default, so identity signs and ledger verifies with matching material. The canonical digest implementations in both services already matched, so no change was needed there.
